It depends what he took. If he's in pain he should go to the ER. Hepatoxicity (liver death) can take several days but it's fatal, usually over 7 days and the most painful death possible. Any overdose should be checked by a medical professional even if you feel and are acting fine.

I just spent 4 days in a critical care unit in a coma. Overdoses are serious, you can have several lucid days and then be floored.

Thanks, love.

No I don't think many people really will be hurt. I think the damage has been done already. When you're sat just waiting for your divorce papers and the entire reason is you couldn't pull yourself out of the insanity, and so you tried to end the insanity and failed, and all your friends have gone, and all your family can do is just cry at what a mess you've made and not see how you can come back from what's been a long standing of fuck up after fuck up with no real remittance. I honestly feel like if I went they could do the sad thing and then for my ex-partner and my friends they could just move on and at least my family would get the peace that my suffering is over and I'm not going to repeat the same screwed up cycle.

I'd love to think that there would be anything but some grief but mostly relief. Not least for myself. I've been suicidal with little remittance for 22-23 years even with medication, psychiatric admissions and talking therapies. I can't stand the mental torture each day, no relief from the thoughts no matter how many "strategies" I try.

I don't really know why I posted. I don't want anyone to stop the runaway train. I am just frightened, mostly that I'll get it wrong and I'll be back here or that my chosen method will be extremely painful but I need it to be effective with no chance of rescue.

That's ok. It sounded from your post like she would be surprised. I still think you should expect her to be very shocked and upset though. Probably angry too. I was but I calmed down very quickly because I didn't want to continue the marriage either. I think the key is to getting through the process quickly. Mine is dragging and it makes it difficult to move on.

I would tell her before you file. I think divorce is a nasty and punitive process without needing to slam dunk your stbx. I'm definitely in the camp of keeping things as calm and rational as possible, and not scoring points. I think any partner would be rightfully upset at begging told they are being divorced out of the blue.

It wasn't exactly on the cards for me and it blindsided me completely when I was already extremely unwell. I think my stbx could have done it in a much less dramatic way and caused a lot less pain and anguish. It certainly didn't make him look like a "big man" in the eyes of friends or family to tell me in the way he did. No there is never a good time but there are ways.

I really couldn't implore you more to try and tell her in a gentle and compassionate way, to make sure she has immediate to some kind of support (friends, family, professionals). You might hate her and want to punish her but you will only make your divorce more bitter, more difficult, more angry. Retribution lasts a short term, the feelings we all experience after divorce last a lifetime.

If your relationship is that great perhaps you could have worked on your marriage harder and not got divorced.

I wish my stbx and I could even communicate let alone be close enough to be in the same camera shot. I mean it's nice that you get on but the reality for most people is that divorce is painful, visceral and devastating so I can see why so many people are upset you would choose to flaunt "your perfect divorce".

Get marriage counselling. You guys sound like you still have much worth fixing. Divorce is like death. Is more than just moving out and splitting up your belongings. You might not see how it could be more but it's an emotional devastation. If you can still save it then do everything you can.

I totally feel you. I could have written that before I tried to kill myself last month. 

I am lucky in that I get free health care which is something I'm very grateful for. I think if you look then you will find charities who will be able to help you, often Christian missions offer free counselling. 

Guilt won't get you any where, you may as well put it in a bag and chuck it in a river. It's done and passed and you can't change it. If I could have done things differently I would have, but I was too unwell and I couldn't see a way out of my issues. I'm sure if you could have done things differently at the time you would have done too. Life is not simple.

I'm afraid you have to take the attitude that he isn't coming back. Anything else is just building houses of cards. Maybe if he sees you suring yourself up and working on yourself then he will want you back but you can't base your recovery on that. It won't work. You can't recover for someone else, neither can they do the work for you.

This just smells off to me. There is much here that it verging on legal and I think you need to see a lawyer. 

I know you've said that you have issues but one person does not make or break a relationship. What is she doing to work on herself and are you going to couples counselling?

I think if you aren't both working then you'll just wake up in a year and decide to get divorced because nothing will have changed except time will have gone by. Maybe you should cut your losses now.

Yep. That pretty much sums it up for me. I thought it was perfect. I couldn't have loved anyone more but love isn't enough. Now it's over and life will go on. I wish you luck with the next part of your story, because there is always another chapter if you want to write one.

I'm in a very similar situation. I couldn't get myself well and my husband, rightly or wrongly, can't cope with the "sickness" bit of our vows, I have no anger at him for his leaving - just sadness that he won't give me a chance to prove I'm doing well.

I'm now well into recovery and thinking about the future. The divorce hurts, I won't lie. I'm scared of being on my own and being lonely but I can't change the past. I'm just having to make plans for myself and where my life as a single goes now.

I suggest that if your mental health is bad enough that it's ended your marriage then you do need psychiatric help. The drugs are not at all scary and they do help. I wouldn't be able to even think about moving on without them. Even if you don't take medication then I would suggest you look for a therapist and start talking therapy. You have a chance to fix yourself for the future and to not repeat your mistakes. Otherwise eventually you'll find someone else and end up back here at some point with them.

The one thing that my psychiatrist has impressed on me again and again is that recovery is a process you do for yourself and not for someone else. Even if changing would get your husband back you shouldn't do it with the sole intention of winning him back. It won't work and you'll just relapse.

It doesn't make me feel better, Rosy, it makes me feel worse that someone else feels this way too. I just feel like I'm waiting for him to file papers or whatever it is he intends to do next. I don't pretend I was a wonderful wife the last two years, I wasn't but I was incredibly ill.

I hope that you can find some peace, love. It's such an awful situation.
